name: Remote appointment setting & scheduling (category)
summary: Calling businesses or customers from home to check their interest and book meetings for a sales team, paid by salary, hourly wage or per booked lead.
whatYouDo: You work through call lists, introduce a product or service from a script, handle objections, decide whether the prospect qualifies, and book an appointment for a salesperson, then log notes in a CRM. Targets are usually daily: one posting expected 10 or more qualified appointments a day.
appeal: Remote postings for people living in Canada appeared in September and October 2026
You book meetings rather than close sales
Some roles are salaried, e.g. $30,300–$55,000/yr, Mon–Fri 9–5 (posted 2026-09-27)
Builds sales and CRM skills that transfer to inside-sales jobs
watchOuts: Phone-heavy, high-volume cold calling against daily targets
Many listings pay only per lead or commission (one freelance role paid $50 per qualified lead with no base), so income can be close to zero
Commission-only listings with big unverified earnings claims are common (one advertised '2k to 5k USD per month' with no base); treat them as a red flag
Postings often require at least a year of cold-calling experience
Calls to consumers must follow CRTC telemarketing rules (registration, do-not-call lists, calling hours); an employer that ignores them puts you at risk
Never pay for leads, training or software to start

training.notes: Postings mention scripts, coaching and team meetings. No formal training route was checked.

compensation.notes: Pay structures differ too much for one range. Postings read on 2026-10-13: salaried $30,300–$55,000/yr (the same posting also lists $38,000–$45,000); a temporary role listing '$20.00–$22.00 per year', apparently a mislabelled hourly rate; and a freelance role paying $50 per qualified lead plus $5,000 if a referred group closes, with no base pay.

reliability.notes: Salaried roles are steady. Per-lead and commission roles depend on lead quality and how many calls convert.

applicationSteps: Prefer roles with a base salary or hourly wage, and get any commission plan in writing
Check the company's registered name and website independently
Ask whether you will call businesses or consumers and how the company follows the National Do Not Call List rules
Do not pay for leads, training or software to start
fitsIf: You are comfortable on the phone, handle rejection well and want target-driven work you can do from home.
notFitIf: You dislike cold calling or need a guaranteed income from day one.

sources.title: Key Unsolicited Telecommunications Rules
sources.notes: Search-summary only. Telemarketers must register with the National DNCL (and subscribe unless exempt), use a list under 31 days old, keep an internal do-not-call list, and call consumers only 9:00 a.m.–9:30 p.m. on weekdays and 10:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m. on weekends.

sources.title: Appointment Setter - Property Print (Indeed)
sources.notes: Full posting read via the Indeed job API. Permanent remote role; applicants must live in Canada. High-activity outbound calls to businesses in Canada and the US; target of 10+ qualified appointments a day. $30,300–$55,000/yr (a second section says $38,000–$45,000). Mon–Fri 9–5. 1 year of cold calling required. You supply a computer, internet, phone and quiet workspace.

sources.title: Outbound Business Development Caller / Appointment Setter - TopTier Cleaning Agency (Indeed)
sources.notes: Full posting read via the Indeed job API. Temporary remote role calling businesses to book cleaning consultations; no closing required. Pay shown as '$20.00–$22.00 per year', apparently a mislabelled hourly rate. 1 year of cold calling required.

sources.title: B2B Appointment Setter – Group Benefits - Kazmir Consulting Group (Indeed)
sources.notes: Full posting read via the Indeed job API. Freelance, performance-based role calling Canadian businesses. Pays $50 per qualified lead plus $5,000 when a generated group closes; no base pay stated. Leads are supplied.
